findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker can inject malicious input that, when converted to an integer, triggers an OS command execution.
findings.assumptions: The code does not explicitly show any command execution, but if the integers are used to index into a command array or similar, this could lead to OS command injection.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: An attacker can input more than 64 integers, causing a buffer overflow.
findings.assumptions: The buffer is declared as an array of integers with a fixed size of 64. If more than 64 integers are input, it will overflow the buffer.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: An attacker can inject special elements that are not properly neutralized, leading to OS command injection.
findings.assumptions: The code does not explicitly show any command execution, but if the integers are used to index into a command array or similar, this could lead to OS command injection.
